title: Former Anti-Corruption Official Among Two Iraqi Lawmakers Jailed for Illicit Enrichment
content:
Iraq's Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court has sentenced two lawmakers to seven years in prison each for illicit enrichment, tying their hidden wealth to an ongoing corruption probe into a senior oil official.

Alia Nassif Jassem Aziz Al Obaidi, known as Alia Nassif, an MP representing Baghdad who built a public profile on anti-corruption rhetoric, previously served as the first vice-chair of parliament’s Integrity Committee. She was transferred to the Finance Committee earlier this year and arrested on corruption charges on June 28, according to Iraq’s official news agency.

MP Ashwaq Salem Hassan has also been linked to the same corruption probe.

The current chairman of the Integrity Committee, Taha Al-Difai, told OCCRP that the sentences were based on the interrogation of detained Deputy Oil Minister Adnan al-Jumaili by an investigating judge. According to Al-Difai, al-Jumaili admitted to having illicit dealings with the two lawmakers.

Investigators subsequently uncovered unexplained cash and real estate wealth that neither woman had reported on their mandatory financial disclosures, which officials must file within three months of taking office.
